sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: We've all done it.
sentences.zh: 我们都做过这种事。

sentences.en: You go to the store for a pair of socks and come out with a mega pack of soda.
sentences.zh: 你去商店买一双袜子，结果买了一大箱苏打水出来。

sentences.en: You go out to get shampoo and come back with a fancy razor.
sentences.zh: 你出门去买洗发水，回来时带了一把昂贵的剃须刀。

sentences.en: It's hard to stick to what's on your liSt. I challenge you to go to Ikea and leave with
sentences.zh: 很难坚持只买清单上的东西。我敢打赌你去宜家时

sentences.en: only the thing for which you game.
sentences.zh: 绝对做不到只买你本来打算买的那样东西。

sentences.en: Just try to buy a lamp without buying a cutting board.
sentences.zh: 试着买一盏台灯而不顺便买一块切菜板吧。

sentences.en: It can't be done.
sentences.zh: 这根本不可能做到。

sentences.en: You absolutely knew this, but retail spaces are designed to do this to you.
sentences.zh: 你心里其实很清楚，零售空间的设计就是为了让你这样做。

sentences.en: The store is trying to look so beautiful, so welcoming, the item so enticingly displayed
sentences.zh: 商店极力装点得无比美丽、热情好客，商品以如此庞大的数量

sentences.en: in such vast quantity that you cannot help but be drawn in and then drawn towards something you
sentences.zh: 诱人地陈列着，以至于你情不自禁地被吸引进去，进而被你

sentences.en: don't need.
sentences.zh: 根本不需要的东西所吸引。

sentences.en: This is the Gruen Effect.
sentences.zh: 这就是格鲁恩效应。

sentences.en: The Gruen Effect, or sometimes called the Gruen Transfer,
sentences.zh: 格鲁恩效应，有时也被称为格鲁恩转移，

sentences.en: it's that moment when you walk into a store and the design of the store is so overwhelming and
sentences.zh: 就是当你走进一家商店，而店里的设计如此压倒性且

sentences.en: dazzling that you begin mindlessly consuming.
sentences.zh: 令人眼花缭乱，以至于你开始盲目消费的那一刻。

sentences.en: The Gruen Effect is named after Victor Gruen.
sentences.zh: 格鲁恩效应是以维克托·格鲁恩的名字命名的。

sentences.en: So who was Gruen?
sentences.zh: 那么格鲁恩是谁呢？

sentences.en: He's a complicated, complex, contradictory guy.
sentences.zh: 他是一个复杂、矛盾且多面的人物。

sentences.en: Jeff Hardwick wrote the biography of Victor Gruen, who was born Victor Gruenbaum.
sentences.zh: 杰夫·哈德威克为维克托·格鲁恩写了传记，原名为维克托·格鲁恩鲍姆。

sentences.en: Born in Vienna in 1904, and he is Jewish in Vienna, leaves in 1938.
sentences.zh: 1904年出生于维也纳，是一位犹太人，于1938年离开。

sentences.en: Good call, Gruenbaum.
sentences.zh: 明智的选择，格鲁恩鲍姆。

sentences.en: And makes his way eventually to New York City.
sentences.zh: 他最终辗转来到了纽约市。

sentences.en: Once in New York, Gruen made a name for himself designing shops and retail spaces.
sentences.zh: 一到纽约，格鲁恩就通过设计店铺和零售空间而名声大噪。

sentences.en: And this was a particular challenge during the lean years of the late 30s.
sentences.zh: 在30年代末经济萧条的艰难岁月里，这尤其是一项挑战。

sentences.en: People had no money.
sentences.zh: 人们手里没有钱。

sentences.en: They just wouldn't go into shops at all.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不愿踏入商店半步。

sentences.en: But Gruen figured out how to lure people inside, basically by using amazingly appealing window displays.
sentences.zh: 但格鲁恩想出了如何吸引人们进店的方法，主要就是利用极具吸引力的橱窗陈列。

sentences.en: You would go into these window display areas, look at jewelry or handbags or chocolates,
sentences.zh: 你会走到这些橱窗展示区前，看着珠宝、手袋或巧克力，

sentences.en: and then you'd be tempted and lured into the store.
sentences.zh: 然后你就会受到诱惑，被引入店中。

sentences.en: I mean, that's the Gruen Effect.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是格鲁恩效应。

sentences.en: Gruen argued that good design equaled good profits.
sentences.zh: 格鲁恩认为，良好的设计就等于丰厚的利润。

sentences.en: And he equates those as one-to-one.
sentences.zh: 他将这两者视为完全对等的关系。

sentences.en: If you do more, people are going to stay there longer and spend more money.
sentences.zh: 如果你做得更好，人们就会在那里停留更长时间并花更多的钱。

sentences.en: Gruen started making storefronts all over the country, and he moved from New York to Los Angeles in 1941.
sentences.zh: 格鲁恩开始在全国各地设计店面，并于1941年从纽约搬到了洛杉矶。

sentences.en: Gruen was from the beautiful city of Vienna, which is lined with shops and greenery and places to gather.
sentences.zh: 格鲁恩来自美丽的维也纳，那里街道两旁商铺林立、绿树成荫，还有许多聚会场所。

sentences.en: He saw how most Americans were just riding around in their cars all the time, cut off from the city and from each other.
sentences.zh: 他看到大多数美国人整天只是开着汽车四处转悠，与城市彼此隔绝，也与他人彼此隔绝。

sentences.en: And he knew this problem was even worse in the suburbs.
sentences.zh: 他知道这个问题在郊区更加严重。

sentences.en: The suburbs lacked what sociologist Ray Oldenburg calls third places.
sentences.zh: 郊区缺乏社会学家雷·奥登堡所称的“第三空间”。

sentences.en: Think of home as your primary place, work as your second place.
sentences.zh: 把家当作你的第一空间，工作当作你的第二空间。

sentences.en: And that third place is where you go to build community, to hang out, to simply feel connected.
sentences.zh: 而第三空间则是你去建立社群、闲逛、单纯感受连接的地方。

sentences.en: Gruen wanted to give the American suburbs that third place.
sentences.zh: 格鲁恩想要给美国郊区提供那种第三空间。

sentences.en: The image of living in closer communication with other people.
sentences.zh: 一种与其他人进行更紧密交流的生活意象。

sentences.en: The image of having the possibility from walk to one place to another.
sentences.zh: 一种能够步行从一个地方走到另一个地方的可能性的意象。

sentences.en: That's archival footage of Gruen from the University of Wyoming.
sentences.zh: 那是怀俄明大学保存的格鲁恩的档案录像。

sentences.en: The image of participating in events outside of your own little house has become a desirable factor.
sentences.zh: 参与自己小房子以外活动的意象已经成了一个令人向往的因素。

sentences.en: Victor Gruen imagined designing an environment full of greenery and shops, an indoor plaza, a modern forum,
sentences.zh: 维克托·格鲁恩构想设计一个充满绿植和商店的环境，一个室内广场，一个现代化的论坛，

sentences.en: an island of connection in the middle of the sprawl, one that would only be accessible to pedestrians.
sentences.zh: 一个坐落在城市无序扩张之中的连接之岛，一个只对行人开放的地方。

sentences.en: Because, oh man, Victor Gruen hated cars.
sentences.zh: 因为，天哪，维克托·格鲁恩太讨厌汽车了。

sentences.en: He rants and raves against cars continually.
sentences.zh: 他不断地痛骂和抨击汽车。

sentences.en: One technological event has swamped us.
sentences.zh: 有一场技术事件把我们淹没了。

sentences.en: That is the advent of the rubber-wheeled vehicle, the private car, the truck, the trailer, as means of mass transportation.
sentences.zh: 那就是作为大众运输工具的胶轮车辆、私家车、卡车和拖车的出现。

sentences.en: And their threat to human life and health is just as great as that of the exposed sewer.
sentences.zh: 它们对人类生命和健康的威胁，和露天下水道不相上下。

sentences.en: It's hard to understand him with the tape hiss and the accent, but what Gruen is saying there is.
sentences.zh: 由于磁带的杂音和口音，很难听懂他在说什么，但格鲁恩在那里说的是。

sentences.en: The threat of cars to human life and health is as great as the exposed sewer.
sentences.zh: 汽车对人类生命和健康的威胁与露天下水道一样大。

sentences.en: So Gruen's objective was to get people to park their cars far away from these third places and walk and stroll within them.
sentences.zh: 因此，格鲁恩的目标是让人把车停在远离这些第三空间的地方，然后在其中步行漫步。

sentences.en: As Gruen saw it, his structure would be an architectural panacea.
sentences.zh: 在格鲁恩看来，他的建筑将是一剂建筑学上的万灵药。

sentences.en: It would remedy environmental, commercial, and sociological problems with the creation of a single building.
sentences.zh: 它将通过建造单一的建筑来解决环境、商业和社会学方面的问题。

sentences.en: And so Gruen presented his solution for America.
sentences.zh: 于是，格鲁恩提出了他为美国准备的解决方案。

sentences.en: The shopping mall.
sentences.zh: 购物中心。

sentences.en: Gruen actually wanted the shopping mall to be more than just shops.
sentences.zh: 格鲁恩实际上希望购物中心不仅仅只有商店。

sentences.en: He wants them to be mixed use.
sentences.zh: 他希望它们是综合用途的。

sentences.en: He wants apartments and offices or medical centers attached to the shopping center.
sentences.zh: 他希望购物中心附带公寓、办公室或医疗中心。

sentences.en: He makes cases to have child care facilities, libraries, bomb shelters, a whole range of different functions.
sentences.zh: 他提出设立托儿所、图书馆、防空洞等一系列不同的功能设施。

sentences.en: And Gruen dreamed and wrote about the enclosed shopping center way before he ever built one.
sentences.zh: 早在建造封闭式购物中心之前，格鲁恩就梦想并撰文探讨过它。

sentences.en: Until he finally lands a commission for the very first indoor, climate-controlled shopping center.
sentences.zh: 直到他最终接到了第一个室内、恒温购物中心的委托。

sentences.en: In Adina, Minnesota, a place not known for its welcoming climate.
sentences.zh: 在明尼苏达州的埃迪纳，一个并不以气候宜人著称的地方。

sentences.en: Southdale represents an entirely new and dramatic concept in retail merchandising.
sentences.zh: 绍代尔代表了零售商业领域一个全新且戏剧性的概念。

sentences.en: Southdale Center opened in 1956.
sentences.zh: 绍代尔购物中心于1956年开业。

sentences.en: And it was the mother of all shopping malls.
sentences.zh: 它是所有购物中心的始祖。

sentences.en: Seriously.
sentences.zh: 说真的。

sentences.en: Gruen's subsequent malls were all mostly based off this original Adina design.
sentences.zh: 格鲁恩随后的购物中心大多都是以最初的埃迪纳设计为基础的。

sentences.en: When he's doing the first enclosed shopping mall, Southdale, in Adina, Minnesota,
sentences.zh: 当他在明尼苏达州埃迪纳建造第一个封闭式购物中心——绍代尔时，

sentences.en: what Gruen really emphasizes and what the media ends up celebrating is this massive center court.
sentences.zh: 格鲁恩真正强调的以及媒体最终大肆庆祝的，是这个巨大的中央庭院。

sentences.en: This court is enclosed and skylighted so that not only the stores, but the shopping sidewalks.
sentences.zh: 这个庭院是封闭的，带有天窗，因此不仅是商店，还有购物人行道。

sentences.en: In fact, the whole area in front of the stores is air-conditioned and temperature-controlled.
sentences.zh: 事实上，商店前面的整个区域都是装有空调且温控的。

sentences.en: A year-round climate of 72 degrees.
sentences.zh: 全年保持华氏72度的恒温气候。

sentences.en: For Gruen, he's creating a town square.
sentences.zh: 对格鲁恩来说，他正在创造一个城镇广场。

sentences.en: Southdale Center wasn't quite mixed use, like Gruen imagined.
sentences.zh: 绍代尔购物中心并不完全像格鲁恩想象的那样具有综合用途。

sentences.en: People didn't live in it.
sentences.zh: 人们并不住在里面。

sentences.en: And something like a daycare center or a post office couldn't afford that rent.
sentences.zh: 像日托中心或邮局这样的机构也承担不起那里的租金。

sentences.en: But Southdale did have local shops of all kinds.
sentences.zh: 但绍代尔确实拥有各种各样的本地商店。

sentences.en: And plenty of shoppers.
sentences.zh: 还有大量的购物者。

sentences.en: Southdale.
sentences.zh: 绍代尔。

sentences.en: Tomorrow's Main Street.
sentences.zh: 明天的商业街。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: But from the outside, Southdale Center is not much to look at.
sentences.zh: 但从外观上看，绍代尔购物中心并没有什么好看的。

sentences.en: I mean, it looks like a mall.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它看起来就像个商场。

sentences.en: It's this ominous, amorphous, boxy shape.
sentences.zh: 这是一个不详的、无定形的、方盒子般的形状。

sentences.en: In designing these shopping malls, Gruen ended his razzle-dazzle storefronts and window displays.
sentences.zh: 在设计这些购物中心时，格鲁恩放弃了他那炫目耀眼的店面和橱窗展示。

sentences.en: Southdale hardly has exterior windows at all.
sentences.zh: 绍代尔几乎完全没有外部窗户。

sentences.en: He moves away from the original concept that, in some ways, they're going to attract by being ostentatious.
sentences.zh: 他放弃了最初的观念，即某种程度上它们会通过浮华来吸引人。

sentences.en: The draw now is what's inside the mall.
sentences.zh: 现在的吸引力在于商场内部的东西。

sentences.en: In Gruen's mind, it should have pretty much a blank facade, no signage on it.
sentences.zh: 在格鲁恩看来，它应该基本上是一个空白的外立面，上面没有任何标牌。

sentences.en: And then you enter that space, and then you walk into the shopping center,
sentences.zh: 然后你进入那个空间，再走进购物中心，

sentences.en: and that's that sort of transformational Gruen transfer moment.
sentences.zh: 那正是那种变革性的格鲁恩转移时刻。

sentences.en: Malls are designed as these sort of suburban pilgrimage sites,
sentences.zh: 商场被设计成某种郊区朝圣地，

sentences.en: which, of course, you have to drive to.
sentences.zh: 当然，你必须开车才能去。

sentences.en: It's a commitment.
sentences.zh: 这是一场长途跋涉。

sentences.en: You're driving 20, 30 minutes.
sentences.zh: 你要开车20、30分钟。

sentences.en: You're parking.
sentences.zh: 你要停车。

sentences.en: You're getting out of your car.
sentences.zh: 你要下车。

sentences.en: You're walking in.
sentences.zh: 你要走进去。

sentences.en: Gruen knew that Americans love to drive.
sentences.zh: 格鲁恩深知美国人热爱开车。

sentences.en: So the mall was his compromise.
sentences.zh: 所以商场是他的妥协方案。

sentences.en: You had to walk and stroll once you were inside.
sentences.zh: 一旦进到里面，你就必须步行散步。

sentences.en: But the customers could drive over.
sentences.zh: 但顾客可以开车过来。

sentences.en: So he just hates the automobile, but he never will acknowledge that he's creating these shopping centers,
sentences.zh: 因此，他虽然痛恨汽车，却永远不承认自己正在建造的这些购物中心，

sentences.en: which are largely only accessible through cars.
sentences.zh: 很大程度上只能通过汽车才能到达。

sentences.en: Gruen was right.
sentences.zh: 格鲁恩是对的。

sentences.en: Americans loved driving to his malls.
sentences.zh: 美国人非常喜欢开车去他的商场。

sentences.en: He got commissions for them all over the country.
sentences.zh: 他在全国各地都接到了建造商场的委托。

sentences.en: But over time, Gruen sees that in erecting these malls, these tiny suburban cities,
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，格鲁恩发现，通过建立这些商场、这些微型郊区城市，

sentences.en: he's helping to drain the real cities.
sentences.zh: 他正在帮助掏空真正的城市。

sentences.en: And so for a while, Gruen shifts his focus to urban planning.
sentences.zh: 因此在一段时间里，格鲁恩将重点转向了城市规划。

sentences.en: We want to rescue our cities, which, because we have neglected, are threatening to go to pieces.
sentences.zh: 我们想要拯救我们的城市，由于我们一直忽视它们，它们正面临着四分五裂的危险。

sentences.en: And so Gruen ends up being involved in urban renewal projects where he draws directly on some of the lessons learned in his suburban shopping malls
sentences.zh: 于是格鲁恩最终参与了城市更新项目，在项目中他直接借鉴了从郊区购物中心学到的一些经验，

sentences.en: and proposes bringing them back downtown.
sentences.zh: 并提议把它们带回市中心。

sentences.en: Municipalities hire Gruen and associates to make their downtowns more like malls.
sentences.zh: 市政当局聘请格鲁恩及其合伙人，把他们的市中心变得更像商场。

sentences.en: Gruen turns city centers into pedestrian-only spaces, full of public art and greenery and lined with shops.
sentences.zh: 格鲁恩把市中心变成只允许行人通行的步行区，里面充满了公共艺术和绿化，两旁开满商店。

sentences.en: He made plans for Boulder, Fresno, Fort Worth, Kalamazoo.
sentences.zh: 他为博尔德、弗雷斯诺、沃思堡、卡拉马祖做过规划。

sentences.en: Actually, his plan for Kalamazoo became the first outdoor pedestrian shopping mall in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他为卡拉马祖做的规划成了美国第一个户外步行购物中心。

sentences.en: He even had a concept to turn Fifth Avenue into a pedestrian mall.
sentences.zh: 他甚至还有一个将第五大道变成步行商业街的构想。

sentences.en: He gets Manhattan to close down Fifth Avenue for a couple weeks as a teSt.
sentences.zh: 他让曼哈顿关闭第五大道几周作为试验。

sentences.en: But a city's downtown is not a mall.
sentences.zh: 但城市的市中心可不是商场。

sentences.en: It's not so easily, quote-unquote, fixed.
sentences.zh: 它没那么容易被“修复”。

sentences.en: Not so perfectly designed and controlled.
sentences.zh: 没有那么完美的设计和控制。

sentences.en: Cities weren't going to become the pleasant, sterile shopping environments that Gruen wanted them to be.
sentences.zh: 城市不会变成格鲁恩所期望的那种令人愉快、了无生气的购物环境。

sentences.en: After the riots of the 60s, he's shocked and sort of taken aback by those and was very much unprepared for them.
sentences.zh: 在60年代的暴动之后，他感到震惊和错愕，对此毫无准备。

sentences.en: And I think that may have been somewhat of his reason for the retreat to Vienna.
sentences.zh: 我想这可能在某种程度上是他隐退回维也纳的原因。

sentences.en: In 1968, Gruen moved from Los Angeles back to Vienna, back to the greenery and plazas he had been trying to imitate.
sentences.zh: 1968年，格鲁恩从洛杉矶搬回维也纳，回到了他一直试图模仿的绿地和广场。

sentences.en: But he could not escape his own creation.
sentences.zh: 但他无法逃避自己创造的产物。

sentences.en: There's a shopping mall that's being built on the edge of Vienna.
sentences.zh: 维也纳边缘正在建造一个购物中心。

sentences.en: And he points to that as how that shopping mall is destroying downtown Vienna.
sentences.zh: 他指出那个购物中心是如何毁掉维也纳市中心的。

sentences.en: In Gruen's mind, Vienna was already perfectly planned.
sentences.zh: 在格鲁恩看来，维也纳本来就已经规划得完美无缺。

sentences.en: It didn't need a mall like the broken American suburbs did.
sentences.zh: 它不像那些支离破碎的美国郊区那样需要商场。

sentences.en: As he saw it, his original vision had been completely skewed.
sentences.zh: 在他看来，他最初的愿景已经被彻底扭曲了。

sentences.en: After being in Vienna about 10 years, he gives a speech and writes a paper where he says,
sentences.zh: 在维也纳呆了大约10年后，他发表了一次演讲并写了一篇论文，其中说道：

sentences.en: I refuse to pay alimony for these bastard developments.
sentences.zh: 我拒绝为这些混蛋开发项目支付赡养费。

sentences.en: Victor Gruen, the mall maker, became the foremost mall critic.
sentences.zh: 商场缔造者维克托·格鲁恩，最终成了头号商场批评家。

sentences.en: And meanwhile, America's love affair with malls continued.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，美国对商场的痴迷仍在继续。

sentences.en: Dude, you want to crash the mall?
sentences.zh: 老兄，你想去商场逛逛吗？

sentences.en: What's a pretty girl like you doing sitting alone in the middle of this monument to consumerism?
sentences.zh: 像你这么漂亮的姑娘，怎么一个人坐在消费主义纪念碑的中央？

sentences.en: I know I remember in my own experience growing up in New Jersey when the first mall opened anywhere near me when I was in high school.
sentences.zh: 我知道，我记得自己成长在新泽西的经历，那时我上高中，离我最近的第一个商场开业了。

sentences.en: This is Ellen Dunham-Jones.
sentences.zh: 这是埃伦·邓纳姆-琼斯。

sentences.en: She's a professor of architecture and urban design at Georgia Tech.
sentences.zh: 她是佐治亚理工学院的建筑与城市设计教授。

sentences.en: It was cool to go to the mall, but I mean, literally, it was air-conditioned.
sentences.zh: 去商场很酷，但我的意思是，字面意思，那里有空调。

sentences.en: My home wasn't air-conditioned.
sentences.zh: 我家里没有空调。

sentences.en: My school wasn't air-conditioned.
sentences.zh: 我的学校没有空调。

sentences.en: Today, most of us are spending our days and our nights in completely thermally controlled environments.
sentences.zh: 如今，我们大多数人的白天和黑夜都在完全温控的环境中度过。

sentences.en: A lot of us are craving being able to be outdoors.
sentences.zh: 我们很多人都渴望能够亲近大自然。

sentences.en: In recent decades, our tastes have veered away from climate-controlled environments and away from the indoor mall.
sentences.zh: 在最近几十年里，我们的品味已经从恒温环境和室内购物中心转向。

sentences.en: Mall construction actually peaked in 1990.
sentences.zh: 购物中心的建设实际上在1990年达到了顶峰。

sentences.en: It's been declining ever since.
sentences.zh: 此后它一直在走下坡路。

sentences.en: And by 2006 is really the last brand-new kind of standard conventional mall that's been built in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 而到2006年，真正建造出了美国最后一家全新风格的标准传统购物中心。

sentences.en: And a new product has entered the scene, a kind of shopping center that the ICSC, the International Council of Shopping Centers, calls a lifestyle center.
sentences.zh: 一种新产品登场了，国际购物中心协会（ICSC）称之为生活方式中心（lifestyle center）。

sentences.en: Lifestyle centers started appearing in the 90s.
sentences.zh: 生活方式中心在90年代开始出现。

sentences.en: And they tend to be open air, so you don't have that roof anymore.
sentences.zh: 它们往往是露天的，所以你再也看不到那种屋顶了。

sentences.en: But you have a lot of boutiques and a lot more restaurants.
sentences.zh: 但你会有很多精品店和更多的餐厅。

sentences.en: Lifestyle centers are malls disguised as main streets.
sentences.zh: 生活方式中心就是伪装成主要商业街的购物中心。

sentences.en: And even though they're full of chain stores, lifestyle centers are sunny and walkable and bustling, and kind of what Victor Gruen imagined.
sentences.zh: 尽管它们到处都是连锁店，但生活方式中心阳光充足、适合步行、熙熙攘攘，这正是维克托·格鲁恩（Victor Gruen）所设想的。

sentences.en: And some of the old-style indoor shopping malls are being repurposed.
sentences.zh: 一些老式的室内购物中心正在被重新规划用途。

sentences.en: Several of them are being retrofitted into Hispanic community centers.
sentences.zh: 其中几个正在被改造为西班牙裔社区中心。

sentences.en: Like in Plaza Fiesta outside of Atlanta.
sentences.zh: 比如亚特兰大郊外的菲斯塔广场（Plaza Fiesta）。

sentences.en: A lot of the stores have been cut up into much smaller mom-and-pop small shops selling Western wear, selling quinceanera dresses.
sentences.zh: 许多店铺被分割成更小的夫妻店，出售西部服装和十五岁生日派对礼服。

sentences.en: Plaza Fiesta also has a steady events calendar of performances.
sentences.zh: 菲斯塔广场还有一个源源不断的表演活动日程表。

sentences.en: And this, too, was kind of what Gruen imagined.
sentences.zh: 这也是格鲁恩所设想的那种景象。

sentences.en: These sort of community malls are truly places to gather and spend money in the shell of the failed design.
sentences.zh: 这些社区购物中心在失败设计的壳子里，真正成为了人们聚会和消费的场所。

sentences.en: Most people, architectural historians especially, think Gruen was a horrible architect.
sentences.zh: 大多数人，尤其是建筑史学家，认为格鲁恩是个糟糕的建筑师。

sentences.en: And, you know, I can see where they're coming from.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我能理解他们的想法。

sentences.en: I mean, his exteriors of his building are uniformly boring.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他建筑的外观千篇一律、十分乏味。

sentences.en: But for Gruen, that wasn't the point.
sentences.zh: 但对格鲁恩来说，重点并不在此。

sentences.en: It was the interiors that were really the point.
sentences.zh: 室内才是真正的重点所在。

sentences.en: Those fountains, the cheesy statues, the elevator music piped in through all those speakers, those are all part of the Gruen effect.
sentences.zh: 那些喷泉、俗气的雕像、通过所有扬声器播放的背景音乐，这些都是格鲁恩效应（Gruen effect）的一部分。

sentences.en: And they helped turn shopping malls into spaces where we felt comfortable staying and spending time and money.
sentences.zh: 它们帮助把购物中心变成了一个让我们感到舒适、愿意停留并消磨时间和金钱的空间。

sentences.en: A lot of the original indoor malls are abandoned now.
sentences.zh: 现在，许多最初的室内购物中心已经被废弃了。

sentences.en: Seriously, like some of them are growing weeds inside.
sentences.zh: 说真的，有些里面甚至都长出野草了。

sentences.en: There's a website that's become sort of a graveyard of dead malls called deadmalls.com.
sentences.zh: 有一个被称为死掉的购物中心墓地的网站叫 deadmalls.com。

sentences.en: Users can log on and submit stories of the dead malls in their towns.
sentences.zh: 用户可以登录并提交他们城镇中消亡的购物中心的故事。

sentences.en: There are around 450 malls listed there, submitted as sort of oral histories.
sentences.zh: 那里大约列出了450个购物中心，作为口述历史提交上来。

sentences.en: In particular, what's interesting, I think, about deadmalls.com is how nostalgic a lot of this is.
sentences.zh: 特别是，我认为 deadmalls.com 最有趣的地方在于其中包含的怀旧情愫。

sentences.en: And it does make sense.
sentences.zh: 这也是合乎情理的。

sentences.en: I mean, in so many suburban communities, the mall became the de facto town center.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在那么多的郊区社区里，购物中心成了事实上的市中心。

sentences.en: It was really the center of social life other than the school.
sentences.zh: 除了学校之外，它确实是社交生活的中心。

sentences.en: I would be very sad if all of Victor Gruen's malls were demolished.
sentences.zh: 如果维克托·格鲁恩的所有购物中心都被拆毁，我会非常难过。

sentences.en: We should certainly work to preserve at least one.
sentences.zh: 我们当然应该努力至少保留一个。

sentences.en: The most famous mall in Minnesota may be the Mall of America, with its roller coaster, its zipline, its aquarium, and water park.
sentences.zh: 明尼苏达州最著名的购物中心也许是美国商城（Mall of America），它有过山车、高空滑索、水族馆和水上乐园。

sentences.en: But the most architecturally significant mall, its grandfather, is the one that's just a 12-minute drive away in Edina.
sentences.zh: 但最具建筑意义的购物中心、它的鼻祖，则是驱车仅12分钟即可到达的埃迪纳（Edina）的那家。

sentences.en: Jeff Hardwick's book is called Mallmaker, Victor Gruen, Architect of an American Dream.
sentences.zh: 杰夫·哈德威克（Jeff Hardwick）的书名为《造城者：美利坚梦想的建筑师维克托·格鲁恩》（Mallmaker, Victor Gruen, Architect of an American Dream）。

sentences.en: And Ellen Dunham-Jones' book is called Retrofitting Suburbia.
sentences.zh: 而埃伦·邓汉姆-琼斯（Ellen Dunham-Jones）的书名为《改造郊区》（Retrofitting Suburbia）。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Claire Doherty for research help.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢克莱尔·多尔蒂（Claire Doherty）提供的研究帮助。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Avery Truffleman with Katie Mingle, Sam Greenspan, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 本周的《99%无形》（99% Invisible）由艾弗里·特拉夫曼（Avery Truffleman）制作，合作者包括凯蒂·明格（Katie Mingle）、萨姆·格林斯潘（Sam Greenspan）以及我，罗曼·马尔斯（Roman Mars）。

sentences.en: We are a project of 91.7 KALW San Francisco and produced out of the offices of ArcSign, an architecture and interiors firm in beautiful, downtown, mall-free,
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山 91.7 KALW 广播电台的项目，由 ArcSign 的办公室制作出品，ArcSign 是一家建筑与室内设计公司，坐落于美丽、市中心、没有购物中心，

sentences.en: but lifestyle center-rich Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 但生活方式中心丰富的加利福尼亚州奥克兰市。

sentences.en: You can find the show and like the show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 你可以在 Facebook 上找到并关注这个节目。

sentences.en: You can follow my international travels on Twitter, at Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 你可以在 Twitter 上关注我的国际旅行，账号是 @Roman Mars。

sentences.en: We're on Tumblr, Spotify, and Instagram, too.
sentences.zh: 我们也在 Tumblr、Spotify 和 Instagram 上。

sentences.en: But over 160 episodes of 99% Invisible are waiting for you at 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 不过，在 99pi.org 上有超过 160 期《99%无形》的节目在等着你。

sentences.en: Radiotopia.
sentences.zh: Radiotopia。
